fields.hero_prompt: Build an artwork approval process for my packaging team that sends each label proof to design, regulatory, and brand reviewers in order.

faq_plan.q: What is an artwork approval process?
How do I create an artwork approval process?

plan.angle: The top results are proofing-software vendors and guides that list the generic stages (upload, review, annotate, revise, sign off, release). This page shows the approval app a team builds around its own artwork: a request form that opens a job, numbered versions that keep their comments, reviewers in a set order with a rule for who must approve which piece, reminders and escalations, and a release step that sends the printer only the approved version. Four real segments carry it: packaging labels, print shop customer proofs, agency client rounds and multi-store retail signage.
tab_stories: Saffronhill Foods sends version 3 of its 12 oz salsa label through three reviewers in order; the design lead and the regulatory reviewer have approved, and brand manager Corwenna Strouden gets a Slack direct message, because the printer only gets the file after all three approve.
Gorsebrook Print Co. emails customer Aurelian Edevane a proof link for order #2316, 48 shirts in 2 ink colors; he approves proof v2 on his phone, and the order moves into the press queue.

Pellgrave Studio's contract with Fellwater Outfitters covers 2 revision rounds on a 6-banner set; when the client asks for round 3, the request waits for account manager Rosmund Delacombe before a designer touches it.
Harrowfield Grocers prints 22 spring signs for 14 stores; marketing approves 18, and the 4 signs that show a price also go to pricing analyst Ottavio Wolstenholme by Slack direct message.
